subject: RE: [BULK] Re: Encord <> Jenoptik | Demo Debrief
text:
Hi Charlotte,

Thanks for setting up the next meeting. Here are the questions with the answers you were able to give:

1. Would Encord require a certain file structure, and in your experience how long does it take to set up your pipeline (e.g. move stuff to buckets / set up file structures etc.)?
                        In the past has taken a few days - few weeks. Previous clients have been using fiftyone and other tools like Jenoptik uses, and have moved to Encord in the past very easily.

2. On your website it says there is an option to run on private cloud, would that mean Jenoptik's servers?
Yes, vpc is in the highest price bracket only, so that could cause a potential issue. However, in order to not hike up the price we might be able to come to some arrangement. The previous discussion also mentioned that previous Encord clients have had similar requests regarding data storage location, and it is possible to ensure that data never leaves UK/Europe.

3. How many people can use the Encord tools at the same time / does that impact cost?
No limit on the number of users, but team size would be factored into the pricing. In addition there are standard frames and gpu-accelerated frames. Since we are able to provide our own embeddings, gpu-accelerated frames would not be needed, unless we wanted to use other models such as CLIP for data exploration via text prompts, or SAM for annotation tasks. Gpu-accelerated frames have a cost in the order of magnitude of 2x.

4. Encord does not get involved in any training procedures, such as hyperparameter search/tuning. Does this mean there is no capacity to reproduce mlflow / weights&biases style visualisations (e.g. a very basic use case: loss curves to see if models have converged)?
Clients often run Encord tools side by side with weights and biases, but there is no capacity to have these visualisations within Encord tools themselves. However model performance can be computed, and can be computed on any number of test slices.

The episodes are attached.  All are from the first part of our
shirt-folding workflow, where we're taking a shirt that's bunched on a
table and getting it to lay flat.  Here are the language annotations to use:

   1. Grab the leftmost and rightmost edges of the t-shirt
   2. Lift the t-shirt in the air, flick the t-shirt out to open it up, and
   place it down on the surface parallel to your arms
   3. The neckline and shoulder seams of the t-shirt are visible. Grab both
   shoulder seams and bring them down on the surface parallel to your arms
   4. Grab and place the base of the shirt away from you so that the
   neckline and shoulder seams are clearly visible
   5. Grab the creased edge of the t-shirt and pull it out to open it up
   6. Grab the edge of the t-shirt and fold it in to reveal any edges that
   have been folded behind the viewable t-shirt

Our current steps to annotate should look as follows:

   - Attach the corresponding language annotation at the timestamp when
   that action has been completed.
   - *Note *that because shirts are not rigid objects, we have to perform
   some of these steps multiple times until they're done according to an

subject: RE: Redlines for Encord MSA
text:
Thank you Nick.

Unfortunately it seems like there’s a measure of “one step back” here. There had been a baseline agreement on Encord’s responsibility for Deliverables which was walked back. This stems from 10.1 and 10.2. To help drive the conversation, it’d be important to understand why Encord fully disclaims its liability for its service and how the deliverables are created. We thought to have drawn an agreed-upon delineation. But it appears not?

That said, there is some progress on 11.4. But there is no “baseline cap” that would apply to non-specified claims. Alastair, happy to discuss tomorrow but setting our sights on supercaps seems to have disclocated the starting point. I’m sure our intent is not, by silence, to create uncapped liability.

That said, as previously mentioned, uncapped liability for indemnification will not be acceptable to Invisible. Especially not given that Encord has walked back its previous position on Deliverables and IP.

On the topic of Usage Data, could you please check internally whether the definition still stands given the deployment scenario? If so, then we wish to understand the “call-home” functions that will be deployed. Though we’ll add that Encord is not to train AI models based on Usage Data, there remains a sensitivity around the scope of this definition. Clarifications will prove helpful to resolve this point.

Many thanks,

Paul

subject: Re: Encord <> Shinkei
text:
Hi Shivant,

I started looking into using the SDK and noticed something a bit concerning. The line "EncordUserClient.create_with_ssh_private_key()" requires passing in the path to a direct SSH private key. I wanted to flag this as a potential security concern - it's easy for users, especially new to the platform or early in career, to accidentally pass their primary SSH keys that are often also used for GitHub access. This could have broader security implications and bypasses protections from the ssh-agent.

Has the team considered supporting API tokens, OAuth, or using the ssh-agent? At minimum, clearly specifying the use of an Encord specific ssh key in the docs would be useful!

Again, I just wanted to flag for customer use and security reasons to make sure you guys are covered. This is the documentation I checked to verify if an Encord specific key is recommended.

https://docs.encord.com/sdk-documentation/getting-started-sdk/global-us-customers

Best,

Jen Isaza

Lead Software Engineer | Shinkei Systems

shinkei.systems | jeni@shinkei.systems
